_comment: Every value the Dashboard shows, and the thing that OWNS it. CLAUDE.md
rule 7: the Dashboard gathers, it does not work things out. If a fact is
first computed on that page, that is the bug, and it presents as two
screens telling reception different things about the same villa.
The nav_canon.json pattern. This table is what the page must read; the
suite asserts the page actually calls each reader, and that the patterns
under `banned` appear nowhere in it. Whichever side a change misses
Adding a value to the Dashboard means adding a row here first. If you
cannot name an owner, you are about to originate a fact on a page whose

reads.value: pre-arrival form state, and the arrival-sheet chips that mirror it
reads.note: Front Desk's three states. Never recompute from `at` or the answers.

reads.value: a guest's dinner answer when no /dinner cell was ever written
reads.note: Arrival night only, cell wins the moment anyone sets one. Reading /dinner alone showed villa 4 grey here while Invitations had it answered, 8 Sep.

reads.value: stays, dinner cells and each villa's pre-arrival, for the day
reads.note: One reader, so this board and the two it summarises cannot disagree.

reads.value: whether a guest has physically arrived
reads.note: Front Desk stamps checkedInAt. Deliberately duplicated one line on this page; see the comment there.
Returns the LIVE node without a date guard - only its menu.json fallback checks. The date and filled-courses guards are menuCheck's, in tally.html.

reads.value: diners with no villa, both shapes
reads.note: Digital replies under /responses with no room, and staff-added ext- keys under /manual. Reading /manual alone lost every externally booked table that came in through a link.

reads.value: how many people a dining row is
reads.note: One head unless the record says otherwise. Counting a pax-less dining row as nought undercounts the kitchen.

reads.value: where a villa stands on tonight's invitation
reads.note: Invitations' own reader. kind 'ready' is still to ask, and a FAILED send is 'ready' - the reconstruction this replaced counted it as sent.

reads.value: which villas are still owed a dinner invitation
reads.note: Keyed by VILLA, written and read by invitations.html. /previnvites is the pre-arrival SMS log, keyed by booking id, and is a different thing entirely.
Builds a LOCAL date from an ISO day, and handles the dd/mm/yyyy the PMS also writes.

reads.value: whether a timestamp falls on the day being viewed
reads.note: With dkey. A stamp is UTC and a day is local: 9:58am on the 8th in Australia is 2026-09-07T23:58Z.

reads.value: a staff member's name against a print tick
reads.note: The tick stores the staff key, so a rename follows it. shortTagFor is the upper-case chip form and shouts inside a sentence.

reads.value: which cards a role may open
reads.note: The app's own keys: resSheet and cleansBoard, not the resBoard/cleanBoard you would guess.

owns.why: The app cannot see paper, so nothing else can know this. The only fact this page originates.

banned.why: Slicing an ISO stamp compares a UTC date against a local day. It read a published menu as not published on 8 Sep, and would have done so every morning before 10am.
